core.title: Close every journey's continuation topology
core.given: A plan declares one or more journeys: each an entrypoint flow router plus the flow routers reachable through continuations.
core.when: The plan reaches CONFIRM (always, for every declared journey, changed or not); also earlier whenever you author or change routes, continuations, terminals, entrypoints, or the user/system flows those routes select.
core.then: Account for every reachable flow router route exactly once: one continuation or one terminal, never both, never none.
prefer: Walk from the entrypoint, listing each (flow_router_id, route_id) with its one outgoing declaration.
Declare an explicit terminal for each route that ends the journey.
At CONFIRM, re-run the closure walk over every declared journey, not only the ones you edited.
avoid: Reusing a route_id inside one reachable flow router; it must be unique.

Any continuation whose source route does not exist, whose artifact does not occur in the linear user/system flow that route selects, or whose destination flow router does not exist; all three are mandatory.
Continuations or terminals on flow routers unreachable from the entrypoint; they are invalid.
Continuation cycles, even intended loops, until an explicit loop construct defines bounded/intentional repetition.
Implicit code-only handoffs or duplicate continuations.
core.why: Flow router bilateral binding closes declaration→runtime→trace for one routing decision only; journey closure makes handoffs explicit, preventing silent gaps, duplicate continuations, disconnected fragments and artifact-free handoffs.
evidence: The journey closure check reports no findings for any declared journey at CONFIRM (confirm-blocking), including journeys unchanged by the current task.

Each finding identifies the journey, flow router, route, artifact, destination flow router and reason; a reviewer checks every reachable route maps to exactly one continuation or terminal, route_ids are unique per flow router, and every continuation is anchored (source route, artifact in selected user/system flow, destination exist).
verification: Static closure check over the plan's declared journeys. Validation taxonomy: family closure; template graph_route_space_closure; variant planner_journey_continuation. Subject kind: journey; phase: CONFIRM; enforcement: confirm-blocking; applies to every journey subject at CONFIRM with no change prerequisite — including journeys unchanged by the current task.
route_key: each route is keyed by the pair (flow_router_id, route_id); route_id must be unique inside each reachable flow router so the topology key is unambiguous.
accounted_route: a reachable route with exactly one outgoing declaration — continuation or terminal, never both.

Reachability is computed from the journey's entrypoint flow router via continuation edges; continuation or terminal declarations whose source flow router is unreachable from the entrypoint are invalid.

Continuation validity (all mandatory): the source route exists; the declared artifact occurs in the linear user/system flow selected by that route; the destination flow router exists. artifact_handoff: the continuation artifact appears in the selected user/system flow's declared sequence, proving the cross-interlocking edge is anchored in the plan rather than invented by runtime code. Re-evaluate whenever route-to-train binding or user/system flow sequence changes.

acyclic_topology: continuation edges may not form a cycle in this version; continuation cycles are rejected until an explicit loop construct defines bounded/intentional repetition, so termination and proof obligations are not implicit.
Each finding reports the journey, flow router, route, artifact, destination flow router and reason for the failure.
Severity 4; disposition: strict — findings block CONFIRM; this rule declares no exception or waiver.

values: selected linear user/system flow sequence changed (artifact added/removed/renamed)

fires: Any task reaches CONFIRM on a plan that declares at least one journey, even if no journey, flow router, route or user/system flow declaration changed in this task (every journey is re-checked).
A reachable flow router route has neither a continuation nor a terminal, or has both.
A route is added to a reachable flow router without a continuation or terminal.
Two routes inside one reachable flow router share a route_id.

A continuation names an artifact that does not occur in the linear user/system flow its source route selects, including after the route is rebound to another user/system flow or the user/system flow's sequence is edited.
A continuation's source route or destination flow router does not exist.
A continuation/terminal is declared for a flow router unreachable from the journey entrypoint.
Continuations form a cycle between flow routers.
doesNotFire: Plans that declare no journeys at all (no journey subject to validate), even when they edit flow routers, routes or user/system flows.

neutralityNotes: The whole convention lives in the ATDD plan model (journey, flow router, route, continuation, terminal, linear user/system flow, CONFIRM phase), which is method-level rather than stack-level, so given/when/then/prefer/avoid/why/evidence and the activation situations carry over verbatim with no stack, runtime, language, path or suffix named. The validation taxonomy labels (family closure, template graph_route_space_closure, variant planner_journey_continuation) are stack-independent classifications of the check and are kept in core:verification, available to other realizations. The only realization specifics are this rule's concrete validator and finding identifiers (journeyContinuationFindings, planner.static.validators.bun), which per the notProfileKeys policy are bunOnly, while core:verification describes the check, its route_key/accounted_route/artifact_handoff/acyclic_topology semantics, its finding shape, and its severity-4 strict confirm-blocking disposition generically. No additional profile keys were needed beyond roles.plan_artifact.kinds, so proposedKeys is empty.
